ideas.title: Counter or fridge? Ripeness first.
ideas.targetAudience: Home cooks trying to use tomatoes at their best while storing cut produce safely.
ideas.whyWatch: The usual never-refrigerate rule skips two different decisions: ripe fruit that will spoil and tomatoes that have been cut.

variants.caption:
Counter or fridge? Start with ripeness — and whether it is still whole.

Whole + underripe: let it ripen at room temperature, out of direct sunlight.
Whole + ripe: use soon. If it will spoil first, refrigerate for a few days; texture and flavor can decline.
Cut: cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or colder within 2 hours. Above 90°F / 32°C, make that 1 hour. Refrigerate promptly; those are maximum limits, not waiting targets.

Storage guidance: Iowa State University Extension, UC Davis Health and FDA; exact sources included in the review packet. Photos: Winston Chen and Praveen kumar Mathivanan / Unsplash. Photos are ingredient context; the cut tomato is an illustration.

variants.caption:
“Never refrigerate tomatoes” skips a useful distinction.

Whole + underripe: counter, out of sun.
Whole + ripe: use soon; chill if it will spoil first.
Cut: cover + refrigerate promptly.

A storage decision, not a fridge loyalty test.
thread:
For cut tomatoes: 40°F / 4°C or colder, within 2 hours; within 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Maximum limits, not waiting targets.

Iowa State: https://spendsmart.extension.iastate.edu/produce-item/tomatoes/
UC Davis: https://health.ucdavis.edu/blog/good-food/how-to-make-your-produce-last-longer/2025/09
FDA: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/are-you-storing-food-safely

Whole ripe tomatoes can spend a few days in the fridge, with a flavor/texture tradeoff. Source: https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/how-to/growing-tomatoes-home-garden

Photo: Praveen kumar Mathivanan / Unsplash.
